drivingQuestion: Why may an acute mourner eat his Paschal lamb at night but not other sacrificial food?
outcomeNote: The mishna's distinction is explained by rabbinic night mourning yielding to karet only

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי טַעְמָא? קָא סָבַר אֲנִינוּת דְּלַיְלָה דְּרַבָּנַן, וְגַבֵּי פֶּסַח לֹא הֶעֱמִידוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶם בִּמְקוֹם כָּרֵת, גַּבֵּי קָדָשִׁים הַעֲמִידוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶם בִּמְקוֹם עֲשֵׂה.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «What is the reason» that an acute mourner may eat the Paschal lamb in the evening? The tanna of the mishna «holds» that the observance of «acute mourning at night» after the day of one’s relative’s death «is a rabbinic» prohibition. «And with regard to the Paschal lamb,» the Sages waived their prohibition because «they did not uphold their statement» prohibiting consumption of sacrificial food «in a situation» in which doing so would violate a prohibition that carries the punishment «of karet,» as is the case with one who neglects to offer the Paschal lamb. On the other hand, «with regard to» other «sacrificial food,» they maintained the prohibition, because «they upheld their statement in a situation» in which neglecting to eat the sacrificial food entails only the neglect of «a positive mitzva.»
